blocks.text:
This was [Child Name]'s favorite park
in all of Grass Valley.
[Child Name] ran in, ready to play.

Swings. Tunnels. Sand.
A climbing wall like a mountain.
The slide looked even longer from here.

[Child Name] did not know 
what to do.

That night, [Child Name] 
sat quietly on the bed.
The big feeling was still there.
"That was scary," said a tiny voice.
A light blinked  beside the bed.

The lights made a path
across the floor.

"Let's look together,"
said the tiny voice.
"This way," said the voice. "Whenever you're ready."
On the quiet path  lay a clue:
Before [Child Name] could peek, voices called from every direction.

"This way!" blinked a star.
"No, this way!" puffed the wind.
"Too many voices make it hard to hear your own,"
And there it was: a quiet path.

One way was smooth and shiny.
It looked easy.
The other was plain and steep.
[Child Name] looked at the shiny path. It was pretty.
At the top, a cave glittered.
The tiny voice echoed through the cave.
The same words glowed on a wall in big, prickly letters.
"Why do you sound mean?" asked [Child Name].
The voice was quiet. [Child Name] remembered.
"Oh. You weren't trying to be mean."
The tiny voice felt warm again.
"Sometimes big feelings come out sharp," said the voice.
"But if you listen close, you can hear what they are really trying to say."

The prickles fell away.
The wall shimmered.
Beyond it, the world was bright.
The tiny voice helped [object pronoun] notice
"I want to see you," said [Child Name].
A trail of feathers glowed ahead.
The forest grew warmer and quieter.

"Listen close," said the tiny voice.
"That quiet is your heart."
In a warm, magical clearing, Owl appeared.

"I am your quiet voice," said Owl, "in a shape 
you can see."
The warm quiet was inside [Child Name], too.
The magical forest grew small below.

Ahead was the park, the ladder, and the 
very, very tall slide.
Owl stayed close. So did the quiet voice.
[Child Name] was back at the top.
This time [subject pronoun] knew what to do.
The quiet voice was there. Small and warm.
[Child Name] looked at the child waiting behind [object pronoun].
Put a hand on your tummy.

Take a slow breath in.
Let it out slowly.
Think of something you'd like to try.
How does it make you feel?

Listen close. Does your quiet voice say
"no," "not yet," or "yes"?
